Q: Node.js quick file server (static files over HTTP) A:

One-line™ Proofs instead of promises

The first is http-server, hs - link

npm i -g http-server   // install
hs C:\repos            // run with one line

The second is serve by ZEIT.co (now Vercel) - link

npm i -g serve         // install
serve C:\repos         // run with one line

Following are available options, if this is what helps you decide.

Q: Flask flask_uploads.UploadNotAllowed error A:

The best way to resolve is to update the IMAGES tuple of flask-uploads's extension.py file. And instead of modifying it directly, you can simply create a variable (image_extensions) with the updated extension like this:

from flask_uploads import UploadSet, IMAGES

image_extensions = IMAGES + ('jfif',)
photos = UploadSet('photos', image_extensions)

Q: I don't understand boolean A:

If you never intend to change the value of a variable, it pays off to mark it as final, e.g. final boolean isLightOn = false. That way, accidentally using the assignment operator (=) instead of the equality operator (==) will fail the compilation, because the value cannot be reassigned.

Q: Parsing Problems in HTTP Web Proxy Server A:

  1. filename = message.split()[1].partition("/")[2]
    This works only for your test URL http://127.0.0.1:8000/httpforever.com (it extracts httpforever.com).
    But a normal browser request for the favicon becomes something like:
    GET /favicon.ico HTTP/1.1 → your parsing produces a bad filename and bad hostn.

  2. hostn = filename.replace("www.", "", 1).partition("/")[0]
    This is unreliable. The host should come from the full URL in the request line (or the Host: header).

  3. You're sending a hardcoded GET / HTTP/1.0 instead of the original path + headers.

  4. Cache file open in text mode ("r") and sending lines — this corrupts binary files (images, .ico, etc.).

  5. No Content-Length, no proper headers forwarding, no timeout handling → easy to hang.
